title: Adidas releases away kits ahead of men’s World Cup, featuring Argentina and hosts Mexico
content:
Sportswear manufacturer Adidas has unveiled the away jerseys to be worn by its partner nations at this summer’s men’s World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada.

In a launch event on Thursday evening in Los Angeles, one of the host cities for the tournament, Adidas revealed kits with a ​clear ’90s-inspired theme.

The reason the German brand is throwing it back to that decade is because this summer will see the return of the iconic trefoil logo, which was last seen on international kits at the 1990 men’s World Cup in Italy.

The unveiling at Lower Grand Tunnel in Downtown, L.A., which follows on from Adidas’ home jerseys launch back in November, includes the shirts of 25 partner federations, including 13 nations who are already qualified for the World Cup.

Mexico​ will kick things off against South Africa​ – whose own away shirts are an elegant green and gold striped look – at the Estadio Azteca, Mexico City on June 11. ​For that opening match, ​Mexico will no doubt be wearing their own famous green jerseys, ​which were part of the November launch. But throughout the tournament, they will have the option of wearing the grey and white design released on Thursday.

It features a subtle geometric pattern influenced by “grecas”, the patterns often used in artwork and architecture throughout Mexico​,​ who are hosting the World Cup for a third time. It has a red and black collar trim which acts as ​its own frame for the pattern of the shirt which seems to be a running theme​ throughout the collection.

This will be Lionel Messi’s last World Cup with Argentina which means the reigning champions’ shirt was always going to go down in history, whether they retain their title or not. This latest away strip is certainly distinct. The main colourway is a black base with swirling blue floral and plant-like designs throughout.

Italy are yet to qualify for the World Cup but should they do so via the European play-offs, which begin next week, they will get to wear a light-blue and white top influenced by the smart suit jackets often worn by the national team at major tournaments. There is even gold in the collar for the four-time winners who have failed to qualify for the past two editions.​ They will face Northern Ireland in their play-off semi-final next Thursday as the last 16 remaining European teams contest for the final four qualification spots.

Jamaica, whose​ Adidas away jersey was launched last month, are still hoping to carve ​out a route to the ​finals through the inter-confederation play-offs in order to wear their​ new Bob Marley​-inspired design. Next week they will take on New Caledonia, with the winning team to face DR Congo for one of two​ remaining qualifying spaces.
